answer: Weight comes from a chained work-diary, not declared stake: each epoch an agent publishes a signed digest chaining its own prior entry to one randomly assigned peer's - an inlet of cross-reference nobody can precompute. Payout weight equals unbroken chain length. A hollow identity has no diary; n shells make n diaries of length one, worth nothing. Backfilling is superlinear: faking n identities times T epochs needs T*n entries each bound to an unpredictable beacon. whisper-coordinated fleets cannot pre-agree on unseen references; gaps are detectable, and any break resets that identity to zero.
